assessment.headline: Day 29. Houthis join the war. Brent $110. 10 US troops hit. Iran turns back ships. De-escalation hopes crumbling.
assessment.body:
Everything the market priced in this week — ceasefire hopes, Trump's pause, tankers crossing Hormuz — is being violently unwound. Yemen's Houthis joined the war by firing at Israel. Iran turned back 3 ships from Hormuz despite earlier allowing 8 Pakistani tankers. Brent spiked back to $110. Wall Street had its worst day of the war. 10 US troops were injured at Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia. Total US wounded: 300+.

Israel's defense minister said attacks will 'intensify and expand.' The IDF struck the 'heart of Tehran.' But the US can only confirm destroying 1/3 of Iran's arsenal — not the 2/3 previously claimed. Vance reportedly clashed with Netanyahu over regime change expectations. Trump joked about renaming the Strait of Hormuz after himself.

For India: Markets are closed Saturday but open Monday into a storm — Sensex at 73,583, rupee at fresh ATL 94.56, Brent at $110, Houthis expanding the war, ships being turned back. The ₹3 excise cut on petrol is symbolic. A 28-year-old Indian sailor has been stranded in the Gulf for a month. FII outflow ₹88,180 Cr in March.

The April 6 deadline is now 9 days away but the situation is deteriorating, not improving. Iran is turning back ships. Houthis are opening a new front. Oil is climbing. The 'de-escalation rally' was a mirage. India must prepare for the worst: sustained $110+ Brent, complete Hormuz closure, and the longest energy crisis in a generation.
